messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty PD12345 fired: db.conn.queue length > 500 (service: postgres-main)

pagerduty: PagerDuty: PD12345 — Trigger: DB connection queue length exceeded threshold. Auto-escalation in 5m unless acknowledged.

alex: acked — I'm oncall. looking now.

priya: grabbing grafana, is this across all regions or just us-east-1?

alex: looks like us-east primary, replica latency okay. primary conn_queue spikes coincide with a deployment at 17:09 UTC.

maria: seeing app 503s in the error dashboard, ~4.7% of requests last 5m. customers: mobile clients and batch workers.

alex: this smells like pgbouncer exhaustion. runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/db-conn-queue

priya: logs from pgbouncer: "SPOOL: waiting for connection slot" and from pg: "FATAL:  remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections"

alex: quick mitigation: 1) disable noncritical background jobs, 2) set pgbouncer_pool_mode = transaction -> session? hmm check runbook.

opsbot: Suggested mitigation: scale read replicas + restart pgbouncer on db-proxy fleet. Manual approval required for scaling.

jordan: +1 to restart pgbouncer on a rolling basis. we should avoid full outage. I'll prepare the restart play: 
```
for host in db-proxy-??
do ssh $host sudo systemctl restart pgbouncer
sleep 30
check pgbouncer-stats | grep busy
done
```

priya: can we steer new traffic to replica while we do rolling restarts? route policy exists: service.routing -> prefer-replica for non-write.

alex: can't fully steer write traffic. but can enable degraded-mode that retries lesser. deploying degraded-mode now.

pagerduty: PD12345 acknowledged by alex at 1719904330.

maria: Customer impact update: main API error rate peaked at 9% at 17:11 but is down to 3.2% after initial mitigations. No major customer SLA breaches so far, a small set of tenants on heavy batch loads hit timeouts.

alex: rolling restart started on db-proxy-01..03 (3 hosts). doing one-at-a-time, checking readiness.

priya: tail of pgbouncer after restart shows accept queue returning to normal: "pool_size=500, used=120, waiting=2"

jordan: replication lag still low <100ms, so read offloading safe. I've applied a temporary traffic-class rule to send noncritical batch jobs to replicas.

opsbot: Autoscaler asked to add 2x transient proxies — awaiting infra lead approval.

maria: notifying CS with brief: "We've got a degraded cluster, rolling restarts of proxy, expect reduced 5xxs. Monitoring closely."

alex: plan: keep PD open until all proxies rotate and accept queue stable <10 for 10m. if still noisy then we'll scale DB or add pgbouncer instances.

priya: quick note: there was an app deploy that opened more DB connections per worker; engineering to revert risky change if instability continues.

jordan: rolling restart finished on db-proxy-01..05. metrics: accept queue back to baseline, connection errors drop to ~0.3%.

maria: final impact: sustained 5xx window ~12m, peak customers affected ~120, recovery in progress.

alex: closing checklist: add postmortem label, capture precise timestamps, attach runbook steps we used, and follow up with infra to look at connection budgeting per service. I'm handing off to jordon for follow-up.

jordan: taking handoff for post-incident cleanup and follow-up actions. I'll create an incident task and schedule a blameless postmortem.

opsbot: PD12345 resolved by alex at 1719904590.

maria: thanks all — good coordination. please drop any follow-up notes in the incident ticket. :thumbsup:
